sections.description:
Definitions

ACT V OF 1973
ACT V OF 1973
BALUCHISTAN
CONTROL ON POSSESSION AND CONSUMPTION OF DRUGS ACT, 1973
An Act to provide for the
continuance of powers to regulate the possession and consumption of certain
drugs in the Province of Baluchistan in the public interest to improve the
health, morals and well-being of the society
[Gazette of
Baluchistan. Extraordinary, 8th February 1973]
No. Legis. 1-52/Law/72.-The
Baluchistan Control on Possession and, Consumption of Drugs Act, 1973, having
been passed by the Provincial, Assembly of Baluchistan on the 12th January 1973
and assented to by the Governor of Baluchistan on the 31st January 1973, is
hereby published as an Act of the Provincial Legislature of Baluchistan.
3. Definitions.---In this
Act unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or context:
(a) "Drugs" for the
purposes of this Act means Barbituric acid, its salt, derivatives of barbituric
acid ; their salts ; compounds of barbituric acid, its salts ; its derivatives
; their salts ; with any other substances and any other substance or drug which
the Provincial Government may by Notification in the official Gazette in this
behalf declare to be drug under this subsection.
(b) "Provincial
Government" means the Government of Baluchis tan.
(c) "Government Drug
Analyst" means a person appointed by the Provincial Government as such, by
Notification in the official Gazette, having the prescribed qualifications as
laid down under the Drugs Act, 1940 (XXIII of 1940).
(d) "Inspector of
Drugs" means a person appointed by the Provincial, Government as such, by
Notification in the official Gazette, having the prescribed qualifications as
laid down under the Drugs Act, 1940 (XXIII of, 1940).

An Act to provide for the
continuance of powers to regulate the possession and consumption of certain
drugs in the Province of Baluchistan in the public interest to improve the
health, morals and well-being of the society
[Gazette of
Baluchistan. Extraordinary, 8th February 1973]
No. Legis. 1-52/Law/72.-The
Baluchistan Control on Possession and, Consumption of Drugs Act, 1973, having
been passed by the Provincial, Assembly of Baluchistan on the 12th January 1973
and assented to by the Governor of Baluchistan on the 31st January 1973, is
hereby published as an Act of the Provincial Legislature of Baluchistan.
4. Prohibition of certain
operations.---(1) No person shall-
(a) possess any drug save as
allowed to the licence-holders to import, manufacture, distribute, stock and
sell drugs under Drugs Act, 1940 (XXIII of 1940) ;
(b) consume any drug save as
prescribed by a Registered Medical Practitioner practising the allopathic
system of medicine:
Provided that the Registered
Medical Practitioner shall keep record of all such prescriptions.

vessel, vehicle or place, permits it to be used for the commission by any

7. Subsequent punishment for
offences after previous conviction.----Whoever, having been convicted of an
offence punishable under section 5 or section a is guilty of any offence
punishable under any of these sections, shall be subject to, for every such
subsequent offence, rigorous imprisonment which may extend to eight years and a
fine which may extend to two thousand rupees:
Provided that the minimum term of

Security for abstaining from commission of offences

ACT V OF 1973
ACT V OF 1973

An Act to provide for the
continuance of powers to regulate the possession and consumption of certain
drugs in the Province of Baluchistan in the public interest to improve the
health, morals and well-being of the society
[Gazette of
Baluchistan. Extraordinary, 8th February 1973]
No. Legis. 1-52/Law/72.-The
Baluchistan Control on Possession and, Consumption of Drugs Act, 1973, having
been passed by the Provincial, Assembly of Baluchistan on the 12th January 1973
and assented to by the Governor of Baluchistan on the 31st January 1973, is
hereby published as an Act of the Provincial Legislature of Baluchistan.
8. Security for abstaining
from commission of offences.---(1) Whenever any person is convicted of an
offence punishable under section 5, 6 or 7, and the Court, Tribunal or
Authority convicting him is of opinion that it is necessary to require such
person to execute a bond for abstaining from the commission of offences punishable
under these sections, the Court, Tribunal or Authority may at the time of
passing sentence on such person, order him to execute a bond for a sum
proportionate to his means, with or without sureties, for abstaining from the
commission of such offence during such period, not exceeding three years, as it
thinks fit to fix.
(2) The bond shall be in the form
contained in Schedule 1 of the Dangerous Drugs Act, 1930 (II of 1930) and the
provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, shall, in so far as they
are applicable, apply to all matters connected with such bonds as it were bond
to keep the peace ordered to be executed under section 106 of that Code.
(3) If the conviction is set
aside on appeal or otherwise, the bond so executed shall become void.
(4) An order under this section
may also be made by Appellate ,or Revisional Court or Authority when exercising
powers of Appeal or Revision.

13. Analysis of drugs.---All
drugs seized under this Act shall be analysed by the Government Drug Analyst or
any person having prescribed qualifications as laid down under the Drugs Act,
1940 (XXIII of 1940) appointed by Provincial Government in this behalf and the
certificate Issued by such Government Analyst or person as the case may be
shall be considered as a conclusive evidence in support or otherwise of the
prosecution.

14. Burden of proof.---Where
any drugs notified under section 3 are seized under this Act in the reasonable
belief that an act to avoid any prohibition or restriction for the time being
enforced by or under this Act has been committed !n respect of such drugs, or
that there is intent so commit such act, the burden of proving that no such act
has been committed or there was no such intent shall be on the person from
whose possession the drugs were seized.
